subject: Feature portability and rollup roadmap for mid-tier upgrade

Subject: Feature portability and rollup roadmap for mid-tier upgrade

Hi Prioym —

We're kicking off evaluation internally on moving Elara from Compact into the Mid-tier plan later this quarter. A couple of asks up front so we can align with Procurement and Engineering: 

- Can Redwood preserve our existing feature entitlements (particularly the advanced reranking and protected model snapshots) for a transition window so we don't lose configured routes?
- We need a clear rollback policy (time window + data handling) if performance regressions show up after the rollup.
- High-level pricing impact (seat vs throughput framing) and an example invoice for our expected monthly tokens (attached usage sample).

We're also sensitive to procurement timing — if we can get a single amends/DocuSign and a note on a pilot discount that would help expedite.

Attaching a redacted usage CSV (Elara_MVP_usage_Q2.csv) for context. Can you loop in anyone on your side who should be at the table for migration constraints?

Thanks,
Stacey
Stacey Morales
VP Product, Elara Labs
stacey@elara.ai

From: priyom_das <priyom@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Feature portability and rollup roadmap for mid-tier upgrade

Hi Stacey — thanks for the note and the usage file — helpful benchmark. High level response and three pragmatic paths we typically recommend depending on risk tolerance and procurement constraints: 

1) Stepwise rollup (recommended) — preserve entitlements for a 90-day transition window. We keep feature flags on, run traffic-slice canaries, and do a staged cutover. Price delta: ~+18% over Compact (seat-equivalent framing) for your current monthly token distribution.

2) Quantized mid-tier (conservative) — move to Mid-tier base but gate the expensive reranking calls into a metered add-on for 30 days. Minimizes immediate bill impact and lets us measure quality. Price delta: ~+10% with metered add-on charge for reranks.

3) Burst add-on only (low-commit) — stay Compact and add a Dedicated-burst pool for peak workflows. No feature portability guarantee; no permanent entitlements change. Price delta depends on peak minutes.

Pilot discount and logistics: we can offer 15% off list on the first 12 months for a 6-month pilot + a 30-day rollback clause if end-to-end SLAs aren't met post-cutover. If Elara can commit to a 12-month term on Mid-tier, we can move to 20% first-year discount (volume dependent).

Next steps I propose:
- I will attach a slim proposal (Redwood_proposal_v2.pdf) with the three options and example invoices for your CSV numbers.
- Kimberly will add engineering constraints and migration notes.
- If Procurement confirms the desired rollback window and discount target, I can prepare a DocuSign-ready amendment and pricing sheet for your legal/procurement team.

Available for a 30m sync today or tomorrow to walk through margins and the migration checklist.

Best,
Prioym Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
priyom@redwood.com
(attachment: Redwood_proposal_v2.pdf)

Adding a few technical points from the Infra/Onboarding side so expectations are clear: 

- "Feature portability" has two categories: entitlement flags (easy) and stateful artifacts (hard).
  - Entitlement flags (rerank enabled, snapshot access) can be preserved at the account layer during a rollup.
  - Stateful exports (KV-cache checkpoints, per-request custom prompts stored as customer state) require either a short export window or running a Dedicated job to ensure cache warmup.

- For Elara's usage profile I recommend a 48–72 hour warmup window for KV-cache-dependent routes; during that time you'll see a modest latency variance. We'll isolate that to a canary region first.

- Migration runbook (stub) attached — it contains a checklist we use for the stepwise plan. The runbook also includes rollback steps (clear snapshot revert + entitlements reset).

We'll support a canary in a single region and a rollback within the 60–90 day guardrail you requested; if Procurement requires a shorter rollback window (<=30 days) we will need an explicit SLA exception and additional run cost to guarantee state mirroring.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.com
(attachment: migration_runbook_stub.md)
